newsitem.title: USA: Genzyme Transgenics expands vaccine trial.
newsitem.headline: Genzyme Transgenics expands vaccine trial.

text.p: Genzyme Transgenics Corp said Tuesday that it has signed a five-year Cooperative Research and Development Agreement with the National Cancer Institute (NCI) to expand research and development activities related to idiotypic cancer vaccines.
This agreement expands phase I clinical trials currently in progress at NCI.
Under the terms of the agreement, Genzyme Transgenics will have licensing rights to the idiotypic vaccines being developed in collaboration with the NCI.
Idiotypic vaccines contain proteins derived from individual patient tumors or from specific types of tumors.

In the phase I trials, the vaccines are being administered after chemotherapy to patients suffering from B-cell lymphoma, a cancer characterized by tumors in the lymph nodes, and multiple myeloma, a type of cancer in which tumors appear in the bone marrow.
Genzyme said that the vaccines have shown early promise in extending clinical remission.
